overview.title: Treasures from an Ancient Sea
overview.p1: Long before the Sahara became a sea of sand, this region was covered by a prehistoric ocean teeming with marine life. Today, local workshops unearth, cut, and polish incredible fossils dating back hundreds of millions of years.
overview.p2: Visiting a fossil workshop offers a fascinating look into local craftsmanship. You can observe artisans carefully extracting trilobites from rock matrices and shaping polished marble inlaid with prehistoric ammonites and orthoceras.
overview.p3: Easily paired with a desert 4x4 excursion or as a stopover between Erfoud and Merzouga, visiting the workshops is an educational and memorable experience for geology enthusiasts and curious travelers alike.

q1.question: Can visitors tour the Fossil Workshops?
q1.answer: Yes, local workshops and showrooms welcome visitors to see how ancient marine fossils are extracted, cut, and polished into decorative pieces.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit the workshops?
q2.answer: Mornings or late afternoons are ideal, avoiding midday heat while traveling between Merzouga and Erfoud.

q3.question: Can you buy authentic fossils?
q3.answer: Yes, workshops offer a wide range of authentic items, from small trilobites and ammonites to large polished marble tables inlaid with fossils.

q4.question: How long does a visit take?
q4.answer: A typical visit to a workshop and showroom takes about 45 to 60 minutes.

q5.question: Where are the fossil workshops located?
q5.answer: Most major workshops are located between Erfoud and the outskirts of Merzouga, easily accessible during a desert 4x4 tour or road transfer.
